result.markdown: --- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [MissingValueCode]{.doc-object-name .doc-class .doc-label .doc-label-dataclass} | Pointblank description: A declared missing-value code, as read from a metadata file. twitter-card: title: >- [MissingValueCode]{.doc-object-name .doc-class .doc-label .doc-label-dataclass} | Pointblank description: A declared missing-value code, as read from a metadata file. title: >- [MissingValueCode]{.doc-object-name .doc-class .doc-label .doc-label-dataclass} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: A declared missing-value code, as read from a metadata file. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} A declared missing-value code, as read from a metadata file. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/posit-dev/pointblank/blob/main/pointblank/metadata/_types.py#L302-L365){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-class} ```pythonsignature MissingValueCode( value, label, category=None, reason=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Many data formats let a dataset declare the values that stand for missing data: the user-defined missing values of an SPSS variable (such as `-99` for "Refused"), or the `missingValues` and `null` markers of a Frictionless or CSVW schema (such as `"NA"`). When [`import_metadata()`](`pointblank.import_metadata`) reads these declarations, it records each one as a `MissingValueCode` in [`MetadataImport.missing_value_codes`](`pointblank.MetadataImport`), a dictionary from column name to that column's list of codes. These objects describe the codes. To use the codes in validation, build [`MissingSpec`](`pointblank.MissingSpec`) objects with [`MetadataImport.missing_specs()`](`pointblank.MetadataImport.missing_specs`), which works from each variable's [`missing_values`](`pointblank.VariableMetadata`) and their labels. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [value]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The value that stands for missing data, such as `-99` or `"NA"`. [label]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : What the code means, such as `"Refused"`. [category]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : The kind of missingness. The readers use `"user_missing"` for values declared in the file. The default is `None`. [reason]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Why the data is missing, if known. The default is `None`. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} The bundled Frictionless Data Package declares `"NA"` and `"N/A"` as missing-value markers for every field. Let's look at the codes recorded for the `amount` column: ::: {#b574b1c3 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import pointblank as pb meta = pb.import_metadata(pb.load_metadata_example("datapackage.json")) for code in meta.missing_value_codes["amount"]: print(code.value, "|", code.label, "|", code.category) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` NA | Missing value marker: 'NA' | user_missing N/A | Missing value marker: 'N/A' | user_missing ``` ::: ::: Each marker is recorded with a generated label and the `"user_missing"` category, since it was declared in the file. A code can also be created directly: ::: {#d6ccd04b .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} pb.MissingValueCode(value=-99, label="Refused", category="user_missing", reason="refused") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` MissingValueCode(value=-99, label='Refused', category='user_missing', reason='refused') ``` ::: ::: Creating codes yourself is mainly useful when you build a [`MetadataImport`](`pointblank.MetadataImport`) by hand to describe a dataset that doesn't come with a metadata file. ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~MetadataImport.missing_specs`) : Build missing-value specs from imported metadata. [](`~MissingSpec`) : Describe missing-value codes for use in validation.
